column2: What does a record’s “🛡 Reliability” score mean?
column3: A score out of 100: the reliability of each fact (a date “about…” counts as estimated), the share of facts with a source, and the 🛡 strength of the link with each parent. The record’s “🛡 Reliability” block gives the reasons and how to gain points. Below 50 (Settings → ⚙️ Check thresholds), the record is “to review before publishing”: filter and column in Lists → People, widget “🛡 Least reliable records”.

column2: How do I make this month’s family letter (💌 Family letter)?
column3: ✨ Treasures → “💌 Family letter”: choose the month and it fills itself in (anniversaries, records and media added this month, a photo, an ancestor in the spotlight). Edit the text in the letter, then 🖨 Print, ⤓ PDF, ✉️ Ready email or 💾 Keep (Lists → “💌 Family letters”). Living people only get their first name and age.

column2: How do I translate a record written in Latin?
column3: In the transcription workshop, “🌐 Translate” (next to “Reading help”) shows the word-by-word right away: formulas in green, dictionary words in blue, numbers as figures. If the in-depth reading (Ollama) is installed, the full translation appears alongside and the two readings are compared. “📋 Keep in the transcription” stores the translation with the record.

column2: How do I have a cousin review a branch?
column3: Settings → Export → “📤 Share with the family…” with the box “🖊 Ask for a review” (or record → ⋯ → “🖊 Have this branch reviewed…”). Your cousin ticks “agree” or “wrong” on each fact and sends you back a .json file. Import it in Questions for relatives → “⤒ Import the answers”, then ✓ Accept, ✕ Refuse or Later for each fact; “↶ Undo” undoes everything.

column2: Why does the export say some records are “to review before publishing”?
column3: Before the GEDCOM “For sharing” and “🌐 For Geneanet”, the app counts the records whose 🛡 Reliability score is below the threshold (without living people or confidential records). “See them” shows them in Lists → People, “Leave them out” removes them from the file, “Export anyway” keeps everything.
